To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the flicker levels for a single 200 MW furnace are in the range of 0.5% - 0.8% of the voltage magnitude, and that the flicker level for two furnaces operating simultaneously is approximately 1.0% of the voltage, with a maximum of 1.3%.

the flicker levels for two furnaces are approximately 2.3 times the levels for one furnace, and that a 20% increase in short-circuit capacity at the substation will reduce the unweighted RMS flicker by 50%.
the unweighted RMS fluctuation envelope for a single furnace is 1.4% of the RMS line voltage magnitude and that the unweighted flicker for two furnaces is 1.8% of the RMS magnitude.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model for the prediction of flicker caused by arc furnaces.
the development and evaluation of a dynamic model for an AC arc furnace that is capable of predicting flicker.
the following issues: 1) The arc dynamics of an AC arc furnace during the initial portions of melt cycle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the system can handle both furnaces in operation without flicker violations, and the flicker violations with one furnace in operation can be eliminated by increasing the short circuit capacity of the 230 kVI substation.

flicker concerns can be addressed by increasing the short circuit level at the substation to 100% of the present level, which is the minimum required to maintain system stability with the present one-furnace operation.
the proposed system changes will not result in any significant increase of the worst flicker condition at any point in the system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
flicker levels are acceptable for all cases considered, but that flicker levels will be higher when two furnaces are operating simultaneously.
the flicker levels for the proposed system with two furnaces in service are not expected to exceed those of the present system with one furnace.
flicker levels will be acceptable for both one and two furnace operation, even for the most pessimistic assumptions about system strength.
The main takeaway from our work is that
flicker levels can be kept within the limits specified in IEC 61000-4-15 with one and two furnces in operation, but the flicker levels are higher for two furnaces in parallel.
the system strength has a significant influence on flicker levels.
the flicker concerns associated the two furnace operation can be mitigated with system changes that will also improve the overall power quality.
